theorem_title: The thirteen-row YAH cancellation leaves only a negative $ff$ coefficient
natural_language_statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be the seven-symbol YAH alphabet and $C$ its fixed thirteen-row unlabelled certificate. For an adjacent-symbol pair $e\in\Sigma^2$, let $\delta(r,e)$ be the number of occurrences of $e$ on the full left word of row $r$ minus its number on the full right word. With the stored multiplier $a$ of each certificate entry,

$$\forall e\in\Sigma^2,\qquad\sum_{(a,r)\in C}a\,\delta(r,e)=\begin{cases}-1,&e=(f,f),\\0,&e\ne(f,f).\end{cases}$$

The Lean statement compares the two coefficient lists over the enumeration of all symbol pairs. This exact integer identity isolates the repeated $ff$ edge for subsequent potential arguments.
